title: Microsoft Copilot Studio: workflow agent node can return generated files
summary: Hold: the spending guidance omits that an environment-group rule can lock the tenant-capacity setting and reject both portal and API changes. The briefing also incorrectly describes the harness documentation as conversation-only, although it explicitly covers workflows.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption-based, metered in Copilot Credits, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits. Creating and using agents, workflows, and apps consumes credits based on usage and rate of consumption.

claims.claim: Using, building, testing and evaluating an agent might consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action they execute.
claims.quote: Workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action they execute.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness credits cover LLM tokens, tools and the harness itself.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Credits are charged to the running agent's environment, using prepaid capacity or its pay-as-you-go plan, not to individual makers or users.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan, and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Caps; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can clear tenant-capacity draw at the environment level or set it through the allocation API without a policy qualification.
claims.quote: If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, you can't override the setting for an individual environment.
claims.fix: Add to controls[0].note and the Caps guidance: 'If a published environment-group rule governs this setting, the environment control is read-only and API updates are rejected with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy; change and republish the group rule, or remove the environment from the group before managing it independently.' The cited allocation tutorial documents this qualification.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A credit rate specific to generating files in the Agent node is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio generating files credits; Copilot Studio workflow Agent node generated files output default enabled prerequisites disable file generation credit rate. Read billing-credit-overview and agent-node-workflow; examined AI Builder rate results, with no Agent node file-generation rate.

claims.claim: Stop usage turns an agent off when it reaches its monthly credit limit.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.
claims.fix: Qualify both occurrences with: 'Limits are not applied instantly; an agent can continue responding for some time after reaching its limit, so allow margin.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity#manage-monthly-consumption-limits-for-copilot-studio-agents, which states this qualification.

claims.claim: An environment allocation is not a spending boundary if tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go remains available.
claims.quote: An allocation isn't a boundary if the environment can continue drawing from tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Clearing tenant-capacity draw prevents use of unallocated prepaid tenant credits, but a linked pay-as-you-go plan can still fund usage.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation. If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts notify but do not stop Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.claim: The environment tenant-capacity control is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: Under Products, select Copilot Studio. Select Manage Copilot Credits. Select the environment. Enter the number of Copilot Credits to allocate. Under Capacity overages, clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the allocation and tenant-pool enforcement setting.
claims.quote: All programmatic examples in this article use API version 2024-10-01. Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put; -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"; @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint. Replace 'The request body sets the TenantPool enforcement rule.' with 'The request body sets allocatedEntitlements[].enforcementRules with ruleType TenantPool and enabled false to disable tenant-pool draw.' These are the properties in the cited tutorial.

claims.claim: Agent monthly limits are at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio. Select Manage Agents. Select the agent, and then select Set limit.

claims.claim: The agent monthly limit pane also configures a notification threshold.
claims.quote: Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit. Configure the notification threshold. Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.claim: No API operation for setting an individual agent's monthly Copilot Credit limit is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent monthly consumption limit Stop usage API PowerShell set limit; site:learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/power-platform agent limit consumption. Read capacity management and harness cost pages and govern-credit-consumption excerpts; found allocation and reporting, not a limit setter.
